correctness.rationale: For Omega(n)=2 the square case r^2 forces S(r^2)=r and r≡1(mod9) or r=3. Digit-sum bound r<=18 log10 r+9 gives r<41; remaining r=3,19,37 have S(r^2)=9,10,19, never r. For pq (p<q), quotient prime forces S(pq)∈{p,q}; if S(pq)=q, q<41 and q(p−1)≡0 mod9 give q=3 with p=2 or p=19 and q∈{23,29,31,37}, all eliminated by explicit digit sums. Thus S(pq)=p; converse immediate. Bound p<=9 digits(n) limits p to O(log x) in n<=x. A prime-counting upper bound uniform over p<=O(log x) plus Mertens gives M_2(x)=O(x logloglog x/log x), and Landau gives zero relative semiprime density. Independently checked exceptional cases and generated all 1617 semiprime Moran numbers <=10^6, all squarefree with digit sum equal to smaller factor. This finite enumeration is corroboration, not an infinite proof.
residual_risks: The O(log x) restriction applies to the smallest prime factor, not to the larger factor.
The asymptotic is only an upper bound and does not establish infinitely many semiprime Moran numbers.

originality.rationale: The closest primary literature and published-result searches were compared for statement implication and actual mathematical object, not just titles. Witno 2010 construction n=12p and repunits does not imply that all semiprimes must satisfy S(pq)=p; its conjectural global count does not imply relative zero density within semiprimes. The submitted use of support and modulo-nine exceptions does. The term Moran number equals Niven number with prime quotient n/S(n); searching both aliases and Omega(n)=2, biprimes, products of two primes found no prior exact rigidity under those formulations. Residual risks are retained; inaccessible full text alone is not equated to scientific failure.
